title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Criminals used AI to generate videos and images impersonating a real immigration attorney, then deployed these deepfakes across social media platforms to defraud vulnerable immigrants. The scam operated through fake accounts on TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram that advertised immigration services for payment, with fraudsters conducting follow-up communications through WhatsApp and collecting money via digital payment apps. This is a deployment of generative AI for impersonation and financial fraud, occurring entirely on social platforms with no human verification of account authenticity by the platforms themselves.

The failure happened at the point where social media platforms accepted and hosted accounts using AI-generated impersonations without detection or intervention. Thousands of fake profiles accumulated before being discovered through victims contacting the real attorney's office. To catch this earlier, platforms would have needed automated detection of deepfake content, verification systems for accounts claiming professional credentials, or monitoring for coordinated inauthentic behavior at scale.

Whether the platforms' systems failed to detect the deepfakes, or whether human review of flagged content was inadequate, is not established by the reporting. The criminal actors' methods and the specific technologies they used beyond "AI" are similarly not detailed.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A South Florida immigration attorney is warning the public after criminals used artificial intelligence to steal his identity and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Angel Leal, who has practiced immigration law for over 30 years, discovered that scammers created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles featuring AI-generated images of him. These fraudulent accounts falsely advertise immigration services, including offers of US residency assistance for undocumented immigrants in exchange for payments like $2,200. Leal first learned of the scheme when potential clients called his office, though suspicious activity began last October and escalated significantly over the past three months.

To combat the fraud, Leal's firm hired an anti-piracy company that has removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically start with social media videos directing victims to contact numbers through WhatsApp, where fraudsters send phony contracts and request payments via Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Leal plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scheme and is urging immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and avoid paying for immigration assistance through digital payment apps.
